why: All three checks confirm the finding. (1) QUOTE IS VERBATIM. scheduled-tasks.md:130 reads, in full: "In [self-paced mode](#let-claude-choose-the-interval), Claude can also end the loop on its own once the task is complete. Claude calls the [`ScheduleWakeup` tool](/docs/en/tools-reference) with `stop: true`, which cancels the pending wakeup immediately. If an iteration ends without either rescheduling or stopping, Claude Code schedules one fallback wakeup about 20 minutes later and ends the loop when that iteration doesn't reschedule either. Before v2.1.202, not rescheduling was the only way Claude could end a loop on its own." The claimed sentence is the second of four on that line, character-for-character. The remaining sentences do not reverse it - they add the ~20-minute fallback wakeup and a version note, both of which reinforce that ScheduleWakeup/stop is the current mechanism. (2) OUR STATE IS AS CLAIMED. `grep -rain ScheduleWakeup` (NUL-safe -a) over the whole repo returns ZERO source hits - every hit is in docs/superpowers/ plans, specs and sweep data. `grep -rain wakeup` over packages/ and apps/ TypeScript, excluding dist, returns exactly one line, and it is a comment: packages/server-core/src/sessions/session-cron-service.ts:91 cites the doc line while explaining why CronDelete drops an already-enqueued fire. No tool, no handler, no schema. The session tool registry ends at CronCreate/CronList/CronDelete (tool-defs.ts:1082-1084); there is no wakeup registration anywhere in the 1380-line file. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, both layers. One layer down: SessionCronRecord (cron-store.ts:54-65) carries id/schedule/recurring/prompt/createdAt/lastFiredAt and NO per-task no-jitter flag, so cronJitterOffsetMs has nothing to exempt a dynamic loop with - the claim's sub-detail holds. One layer up: there is no /loop host for the tool to serve. The bundled-skill directory ships exactly two skills, plugin-creator and skill-creator; there is no loop skill, no loop.md reader, and no built-in command tier to hang one on. So this is NOT the 'unwired identifier, consequence already handled upstream' shape - the upstream is missing too. Nor is it the sibling-subsystem mix-up: the durable scheduler in packages/shared/src/automations/ has no wakeup concept either, and the cron half named in the same doc page IS at parity (5-field dialect, 8-char ids, 50-cap, 7-day expiry, ID-derived jitter, once-a-second tick, symlink refusal, kill switch). NOT AN OWNER DECISION AND NOT A PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. ScheduleWakeup is not among the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (those are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, and listSessionSummaries/listSessions) - none touch scheduling, and section 3 is a 'do not fix' list, a different category from this. It is also unrelated to the fork's deliberate product differences: nothing about subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or the NESSY_ rename bears on a self-paced loop. What the repo actually recorded is the OPPOSITE of a closed decision: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:152-210, Task 4, dispositions it as 'documented, not implemented - requires /loop, which is not in this slice', explicitly says 'This is NOT the Pi-impossibility category', and costs the follow-up at four tasks (bundled-command tier, fixed-interval /loop, loop.md, then the self-paced loop and ScheduleWakeup itself including the per-task no-jitter flag). The parity audit row R27 carries the same string. An open, costed, tracked gap is still a gap.
